about: The first prayer of the Canon. Through Jesus Christ, the priest asks the Father to accept the offerings and to grant the Church peace, protection, unity and governance. He names the Pope, the local bishop and the faithful who keep the Catholic faith.

s01.narrative: After the Preface the priest raises and joins his hands slightly, lifts his eyes to heaven and lowers them at once. The priest then bows low before the altar and rests his hands upon it.

s02.translation: To You, therefore, most merciful Father, we make humble prayer and petition through Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord:

s03.narrative: The priest kisses the altar and joins his hands before his breast.

s05.narrative: Three signs of the cross together over the Host and the chalice.

s06.translation: these gifts, these offerings, these holy and unblemished sacrifices,

s07.narrative: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

s08.translation: which we offer You firstly for Your holy catholic Church. Be pleased to grant her peace, to guard, unite and govern her throughout the whole world,

s09.translation: together with Your servant our Pope and our Bishop, and all those who, holding to the truth, hand on the catholic and apostolic faith.

w001.function: Accusative object of “rogámus” (w013) and “pétimus” (w015), placed at the prayer's beginning.

w002.function: Connects this prayer with the preceding liturgy: “therefore”.

w003.function: A superlative in the vocative, sharing its case with “Pater” (w004).

w004.function: Vocative. “Te” (w001), “rogámus” (w013) and “pétimus” (w015) are addressed to the Father.

w008.function: In apposition to “Christum” (w007), and so accusative.

w012.function: A nominative plural adjective referring to the unstated “we”: “we, the suppliants”.

w016.function: An older form of ut. Not the infinitive of utor (to use), though it is spelt the same.

w017.function: In the phrase “accépta habére”: “to regard as accepted”. It agrees with “dona” (w022), “múnera” (w024) and “sacrifícia” (w027).

w021.function: The first of three occurrences of “hæc” at which the priest signs the cross over the Host and chalice.

w030.function: In primis is a fixed adverbial phrase meaning “first of all”. No gender is therefore assigned here.

w031.function: An accusative neuter plural relative referring to “dona” (w022), “múnera” (w024) and “sacrifícia” (w027).

w039.function: Feminine accusative singular, referring to “Ecclésia” (w035). It is the object of the following four infinitives.

w045.function: “Dignéris” governs the four infinitives that precede it.

w046.function: It agrees with “orbe” (w047). The phrase “toto orbe terrárum” expresses place without the preposition in.

w048.function: A genitive plural depending on “orbe” (w047). The whole phrase means the whole world.

w049.function: An adverb in the phrase “una cum”: together with.

w056.function: An ablative after “cum” (w050). Here it is a title for the local bishop.

w057.function: It agrees with “Antístite” (w056). The missal provides for the local bishop's name here.

w060.function: With “ómnibus” (w059), it forms an ablative plural phrase: with all the orthodox.

w066.function: An ablative plural after “una” (w049) and “cum” (w050). With “fídei” (w065): those who profess the faith.
